security_concerns_to_verify: Permission gating (INV-7/AC3): every route (GET /, GET /:id, POST /:id/retry, POST /:id/discard) is declared via authz_get/authz_post with the :DlqReadRetryDiscard policy key -- confirm Letflow.Plugs.Authorize genuinely runs before any handler body for all four routes (it is wired via `use Letflow.Api.AuthorizedRouter`'s plug(:match) -> plug(Authorize) -> plug(:dispatch) chain, not re-implemented in this router), and that no handler reads any permission/role state itself instead of trusting the plug's Deny/Allow decision.

Cross-tenant-404 (INV-5/AC3): confirm every handler's only tenant input is conn.assigns.scoped_opts (derived solely from conn.assigns.auth_context.tenant_id upstream) -- no query param, path param, or body field is ever passed as a prefix/tenant_id override. Confirm handle_get/handle_retry/handle_discard map both {:error, :not_found} and {:error, :invalid_id} to the identical Response.not_found(conn) call (no distinguishing status/body), so a cross-tenant real id and a malformed/nonexistent id are byte-identical responses.

No data leakage (INV-2/INV-4): confirm dlq_entry_json/1 is a hand-built allowlist (18 named keys) over %Letflow.Dlq.Entry{}, never a raw Jason.Encoder/struct-wholesale encoding that could leak __meta__ or tenant_id. Confirm Response.conflict/2's terminal-state detail string is fixed/non-interpolated (never embeds the entry's actual current status or any other server-internal value) and Response.not_found/1 carries no detail argument.

409 vs 500 (AC4): confirm handle_write_result/2 is exhaustive over Letflow.Dlq.retry/2 and discard/2's actual four-shape @spec ({:ok, Entry.t()}, {:error, :invalid_id}, {:error, :not_found}, {:error, {:invalid_state, _}}) with no fallthrough to Response.internal_error/1 needed or present, so a terminal-state call cannot surface as an unhandled-case 500.

No new permission/policy-key atom invented -- :DlqReadRetryDiscard and :DlqOperate both pre-exist in lib/letflow/api/authorization.ex (REQ-069); confirm this router adds no new clause to endpoint_policy_key/2 or required_permission/1.

Design's own flagged divergence (OQ-3): :invalid_id folding to 404 instead of tasks.ex's 400-for-invalid_id precedent, deliberately chosen because DLQ ids are cross-tenant-probeable UUIDs -- confirm this reasoning holds and is not itself an information-leak vector (e.g. does 404-for-both actually prevent id-enumeration timing/behavior differences, or does it just change status codes while some other side channel remains).
acceptance_criteria_from_requirement: GET /api/v1/dlq returns a body shaped exactly {items: [...], next_cursor: string|null}, and each item's field names (id, entry_type, instance_id, reason, full_reason, retry_count, status, created_at at minimum) match DlqEntry's
GET /api/v1/dlq honors status, source_type, search, cursor and page_size independently

POST /api/v1/dlq/:id/retry and .../discard both require the DlqOperate permission -- a caller holding no role with that permission receives 403, and a caller from a different tenant naming a real id belonging to tenant A receives 404, never 403
POST /api/v1/dlq/:id/retry and .../discard against a non-existent id return 404, and against an id already resolved or discarded return a 409-shaped conflict rather than a generic 500
the route module's moduledoc states explicitly that R-Co's dlq.zig was not inspected in this batch and that web/src/api/dlq.ts / web/src/types/api.ts were the binding contract instead
